fact_text: A breakout happens when price pushes through a resistance level that has rejected it several times; in the example, the third approach broke through on a large bullish candle after two earlier rejections.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, '15. Mastering Breakouts in Technical Analysis | How to Use Breakouts for Trend Analysis in PSX' (YouTube, 2024-11-03)

fact_text: A breakout is treated as valid only when a large bullish candle on heavy volume confirms it; a breakout made by small candles or mostly wicks is not trusted and needs further confirmation.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, '15. Mastering Breakouts in Technical Analysis | How to Use Breakouts for Trend Analysis in PSX' (YouTube, 2024-11-03)

fact_text: One approach enters on the breakout candle itself, with the stop-loss placed below it and trailed upward as price rises; the other waits for a retest of the broken level before entering.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, '15. Mastering Breakouts in Technical Analysis | How to Use Breakouts for Trend Analysis in PSX' (YouTube, 2024-11-03)

fact_text: After a retest, a breakout is confirmed when price holds the broken level for one or two candles, or for two to three sessions, instead of falling back below it.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, '15. Mastering Breakouts in Technical Analysis | How to Use Breakouts for Trend Analysis in PSX' (YouTube, 2024-11-03)

fact_text: A breakdown below a support area on heavy bearish volume suggests further downside, while a bounce from that support area suggests buying interest is returning.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, '15. Mastering Breakouts in Technical Analysis | How to Use Breakouts for Trend Analysis in PSX' (YouTube, 2024-11-03)
